subject: Business
title: The Series A Crunch
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Series A Crunch.

hook.text: Thousands of startups raise seed funding each year. Only a fraction survive to raise their Series A round.

buildup.text: Series A investors want proof: revenue growth, strong retention, and a clear path forward.

discovery.text: The gap between seed and Series A is the valley of death — money runs out before traction proves out.

twist.text: More seed funds entered the market, but Series A capacity didn't grow. The crunch widened.

climax.text: Surviving the crunch means hitting Series A milestones on a seed budget.

punchline.text: Seed money is the easy part. Earning the next round is the test.

quiz.question: What causes the 'Series A crunch'?
options: More seed-funded startups than available Series A capital
Too few startups applying for funding

details.summary: The Series A crunch describes the funding gap where seed-stage startups struggle to raise their first institutional round because investor expectations jump dramatically.
details.whyItMatters: The vast majority of seed-funded startups never raise Series A. Understanding what Series A investors require helps founders build toward those milestones from day one rather than discovering the gap too late when runway is running out.
takeaways: Most seed-funded startups fail to raise Series A due to dramatically higher expectations
Series A investors require proven metrics, not just promising ideas or prototypes
Planning for Series A requirements from seed stage dramatically improves survival odds

faq.question: What metrics do Series A investors typically expect?
faq.answer: Meaningful revenue, often 500K to 1.5M in annual recurring revenue for SaaS. Month-over-month growth of 15 to 20 percent. Clear product-market fit demonstrated by retention. Viable unit economics or a clear path to them. At least 12 months of data showing consistent trends.

faq.question: How can startups bridge the gap between seed and Series A?
faq.answer: Raise enough seed capital for 18 to 24 months of runway. Focus relentlessly on product-market fit before scaling. Hit clear milestones that de-risk the investment. Build relationships with Series A investors early.
